Apply labels to existing columns using a dictionary

Source: R/clean_colnames.R
relabel_columns.Rd

Sets the label attribute on columns that already exist in data. Unlike update_columns(), column names are not changed, so this can be used on any data.frame, whether or not it has been renamed beforehand.

Usage

relabel_columns(data, dict, names = NULL, label = NULL)

Arguments

data

A data.frame-like object.

dict

A data.frame-like object with at least two columns: one matching the current column names in data, and one with human-readable labels.

names

Column name in dict that matches the current column names in data (default "new", which suits data already passed through update_columns()).

label

Column name in dict with human-readable labels (default "label").

Value

A data.frame with labels applied to the matching columns.

Details

Columns in data that are not listed in dict are left unchanged. Dictionary entries that do not match any column in data are reported with a warning. Empty labels ("") are applied, while NA labels are skipped.

Examples

dict <- data.frame(
  names = c("age", "sex"),
  label = c("Age (years)", "Sex"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
df <- data.frame(age = c(34, 58), sex = c("F", "M"))
df <- relabel_columns(df, dict, names = "names")
attr(df$age, "label")
#> [1] "Age (years)"
